factual_claims.claim: Estonia’s GDP grew 0.7% in 2025, while declining inflation and interest rates supported confidence among businesses and households.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating environment: 'Estonia’s real GDP growth in 2025 was 0.7%, according to the Bank of Estonia. Throughout 2025, the turbulence created by the U.S. government in international trade and the resulting uncertainty had a significant impact on the global economy. Compared to 2024, inflation decreased significantly, allowing central banks to continue lowering interest rates, which led to a continued decline in all major base rates until the summer of 2025.'

candidate_sentences.text: Estonia’s GDP grew 0.7% in 2025, while declining inflation and interest rates supported confidence among businesses and households.

factual_claims.claim: However, the six-month Euribor fell to 2.1% by year-end, contributing to pressure on interest income.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating environment: 'For 2026, the European Central Bank (ECB) forecasts inflation at 1.9%, which aligns with the ECB’s long-term target (2.0%). Since June 2024, the ECB has lowered the deposit facility rate eight times from 4.0% to 2.0%. For example, the 6-month Euribor, which is linked to most loans of Estonian companies and mortgage loans to individuals, reached a short-term record of 4.1% in October 2023, but fell to 2.1% by the end of 2025.'

factual_claims.claim: Coop Pank diversified funding by issuing €250 million of four-year covered bonds, the first tranche of a €750 million programme.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Note 17: 'On 13 March 2025, Coop Pank issued covered bonds with a total nominal value of EUR 250 million and a maturity of four years. This issuance represented the first series of covered bonds issued under Coop Pank’s EUR 750 million covered bond programme.'

candidate_sentences.text: Coop Pank diversified funding by issuing €250 million of four-year covered bonds, the first tranche of a €750 million programme.

factual_claims.claim: It also signed an EIB Group guarantee agreement enabling up to €249 million of new business lending; the transaction had not become effective and had no impact on 2025 results.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Managing Director´s Statement: 'At the end of the year, Coop Pank entered into a guarantee agreement with the European Investment Bank Group, under which part of the credit risk arising from Coop Pank’s loan portfolio will be transferred to EIB Group, thereby providing capital relief to Coop Pank and enabling the bank to issue up to €249 million in new loans to businesses. The new funding will be directed toward projects in Estonia that promote gender equality and environmental sustainability. This is Coop Pank’s first synthetic securitization transaction, and also the first such transaction in the Baltics based entirely on the loan portfolio of a single country – Estonia. The capital relief accompanying the agreement enables the bank to issue new loans to Estonian small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and larger mid-cap companies for projects that support gender equality, economic growth, and environmental sustainability. Additionally, Coop Pank signed a loan agreement at the end of the year with the European Energy Efficiency Fund (EEEF), under which the bank will take an unsecured subordinated loan of €5 million at an interest rate of 6-month Euribor plus 3.25% per annum.'

candidate_sentences.text: It also signed an EIB Group guarantee agreement enabling up to €249 million of new business lending; the transaction had not become effective and had no impact on 2025 results.

details.completeness_justification: The candidate summary adequately covers the core material meaning of K1 (profitability metrics), K2 (loan portfolio growth), K3 (deposit growth), K4 (customer base expansion), K6 (funding diversification), K7 (capital ratios), and K10 (dividends). However, it omits the strategic targets outlined in K5, sustainability initiatives described in K8, product/service expansions in K9, the EEEF loan drawdown in K11, and the Management Board appointment in K12. These omissions are material for K5 (HIGH importance strategic targets), K8 and K9 (MEDIUM importance initiatives), K11 (HIGH importance capital move), and K12 (MEDIUM importance governance change). While most HIGH importance items are covered, the missing K5 and K11 are significant strategic and capital items, and the missing MEDIUM items collectively represent notable gaps. The overall coverage is mixed but leans toward 'Generally yes' because the majority of HIGH importance items are present and the core financial performance picture is captured.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is internally coherent. All statements are logically connected and support the overall narrative of business growth with declining profitability. There are no self-contradictions, logical gaps, or organizational issues. Explanations for margin pressure (lower interest rates) and growth drivers (loan demand, economic recovery) are consistent throughout. The progression from profitability metrics to balance sheet changes and external factors forms a clear narrative. While there is a minor arithmetic relationship between segment figures and totals (e.g., loan portfolio components vs. total), the candidate does not claim these are exhaustive additive components of the same total, so this does not constitute a contradiction under the specified evaluation criteria.
